ai.description: *Cnemaspis jerdonii* is a small gecko (SVL ~40 mm) with a brown body, yellow-spotted flanks, and a pale vertebral stripe. It features keeled dorsal scales and lacks enlarged subcaudal plates.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis jerdonii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the lateral folds of its flanks.
ai.habitat: Jerdon’s Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks and rock surfaces at elevations of 600–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Cnemaspis jerdonii is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis jerdonii* is oviparous, typically laying a single, hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cnemaspis jerdonii is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting rocky areas at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
